name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; England rising from low
summary: US flu admissions at a seasonal high not seen since 2010-11; England's flu activity now above baseline
state: US hospitals logged 6,100 flu admissions in the week to 24 Oct, the highest rate for that week since 2010-11, and the CDC forecasts a further rise to mid-November (Nature World News, 4 Nov). UKHSA reported on 5 Nov that flu positivity in England rose to 7.6% and admissions to 2.83 per 100,000 in the week to 1 Nov, still in the low-impact range, with activity now above baseline. An unusually early US season meets Watch; health systems are not reported as strained.
for_you: Flu is rising earlier than usual in the US and is increasing in England. The NHS and UKHSA advise eligible groups to take up the flu and COVID-19 vaccines.
rubric_hit: Hemisphere flu season unusually early: US admissions highest for the week since 2010-11; no VOC or system strain

sources.title: Nature World News — CDC forecasts flu hospitalisations will likely keep climbing through mid-November
UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026 (week 45)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
